unit_label: BRBL Module A unit 2: control over organisation of banks

facts.statement: Licence (courseware): to commence or carry on banking business in India a company needs a licence from the Reserve Bank under Section 22 of the Banking Regulation Act, 1949; carrying on banking business without a licence is prohibited. Companies existing in 1949 had to apply for a licence within six months of commencement of the Act and could continue until their application was rejected. The requirement ensures only banks established and operating on sound lines continue. The Reserve Bank has discretion to grant or refuse a licence and may impose conditions; a court intervenes only where the decision was made on extraneous or unreasonable grounds (Gujarat High Court, Shivabhai v RBI). In considering an application the Reserve Bank may consider defects revealed in an inspection under Section 35 and a refusal does not stop the company from carrying on other business. Under Section 22(3) the Reserve Bank must be satisfied, by inspection of books or otherwise, that: the company can pay its present and future depositors in full as claims accrue; its affairs are not conducted in a manner detrimental to depositors; the general character of the proposed management is not prejudicial to the public interest or depositors; the company has adequate capital structure and earning prospects; the public interest will be served by the grant; having regard to banking facilities in the proposed area and the potential for expansion, the grant would not prejudice the operation and consolidation of the banking system consistent with monetary stability and economic growth; and any other condition necessary to ensure the business is not prejudicial to the public interest or depositors. The Reserve Bank may stipulate a higher capital than the minimum under Section 11 before granting a licence, being satisfied of adequate capital structure and earning prospects.

Foreign banks, on-tap licensing and cancellation (courseware): a foreign bank applying for a licence to set up wholly owned subsidiaries or branches in India must satisfy the Reserve Bank that it is subject to adequate prudential supervision in its home country, having regard to Basel standards; the setting up of a wholly owned subsidiary or branch should have the approval of the home country regulator; other factors include economic and political relations between India and the country of incorporation, financial soundness of the foreign bank, ownership pattern, ranking and rating, international presence, and that the laws of the home country do not discriminate against banking companies registered in India. Licensing policy for universal banks: after the Finance Minister announced in the 2010-11 budget speech the need to extend geographic coverage, the Reserve Bank issued guidelines for licensing new banks in February 2013 and granted in-principle approval to two new banks; the discussion paper Banking Structure in India of 27 August 2013 favoured continuous authorisation; guidelines for on tap licensing of universal banks in the private sector were published on 1 August 2016, covering eligibility of promoters, fit and proper criteria, corporate structure including non-operative financial holding company, shareholding, minimum voting equity capital, foreign shareholding, governance, business plan and conditions for NBFCs converted into a bank. Small finance banks: first guidelines in 2014; on tap licensing announced in June 2019 and final guidelines issued on 5 December 2019; a small finance bank is registered as a public limited company under the Companies Act, 2013, licensed under Section 22 of the Banking Regulation Act, governed also by the RBI Act, FEMA, the Payment and Settlement Systems Act, the Credit Information Companies Act and the Deposit Insurance and Credit Guarantee Corporation Act, and is given scheduled bank status once it commences operations. Cancellation (Section 22(4)): the Reserve Bank may cancel a licence if the company ceases to carry on banking business in India or fails to comply with a condition imposed under sub-section (1) or conditions in sub-sections (3) and (3A); before cancelling for non-compliance it must, unless it considers the delay prejudicial to depositors or the public, give the company an opportunity to take steps to comply. The bank may appeal to the Central Government within thirty days of the date the decision is communicated; the Central Government decision, or the Reserve Bank decision where no appeal is made, is final (Section 22(5) and (6)).

Branches (courseware): under Section 23 a banking company needs the prior permission of the Reserve Bank to open a new place of business in India or abroad, or to change the location of an existing place of business, other than within the same city, town or village; no permission is needed for a temporary place of business not exceeding one month within a city, town or village or its environs where the bank already has a place of business, for providing banking facilities on the occasion of an exhibition, conference or mela or like occasion. Before granting permission the Reserve Bank may require itself to be satisfied by inspection about financial condition and history, the general character of management, adequacy of capital structure and earning prospects and that public interest will be served; it may impose conditions and may revoke permission after giving a reasonable opportunity if conditions are not complied with. Under Section 23(5) place of business includes any sub-office, pay office, sub-pay office or any place at which deposits are received, cheques cashed or moneys lent. For Regional Rural Banks the licence is also given by the Reserve Bank but applications for permission are routed through the National Bank for Agriculture and Rural Development (Section 23, sub-section 4a).

Paid-up capital and reserves (courseware): Section 11 of the Banking Regulation Act sets minimum paid-up capital and reserves for any company wishing to begin banking business; place of business for this purpose means any office, sub-office, pay office, sub-pay office and any place at which deposits are received, cheques cashed or moneys lent; in a dispute about computation the decision of the Reserve Bank is final. A foreign bank incorporated outside India must deposit and keep deposited with the Reserve Bank a prescribed amount in cash or unencumbered approved securities (a larger amount if it has a place of business in Mumbai or Kolkata), and in addition twenty per cent of the profit for each year in respect of business transacted through Indian branches, which may be in approved securities; the Central Government may exempt a foreign bank from the requirement on the Reserve Bank recommendation, and the deposits on cessation of business become assets of the company on which creditors in India have a first charge. For Indian banks Section 11(3) fixes minimum paid-up capital and reserves on a scale depending on the number of States and places of business and whether Mumbai or Kolkata is included, with provisos that for companies commencing business after the 1962 amendment paid-up capital shall not be less than five lakh rupees; the courseware also notes that the Reserve Bank has stipulated specific different minimum capital norms for small finance banks and universal banks in their licensing policy. Capital structure (Section 12(1)): subscribed capital shall not be less than half of authorised capital, and paid-up capital not less than half of subscribed capital; if capital is increased this must be complied with within two years as the Reserve Bank allows. Under the Act, banking companies may issue equity shares or equity and preference shares (perpetual or irredeemable or redeemable) in accordance with Reserve Bank guidelines.

Shareholding (courseware): there is no specified ceiling on a person holding shares in a banking company except the five per cent cap on prior approval under Section 12B and other law; Section 12(2) restricts voting rights: no person holding shares shall exercise voting rights on a poll in excess of ten per cent of the total voting rights of all shareholders; the Reserve Bank may increase this ceiling in a phased manner up to twenty-six per cent. Section 12(3): no suit or proceeding shall be maintained against a registered shareholder on the ground that title to shares vests in another, except a suit by a transferee on a transfer in accordance with law or on behalf of a minor or lunatic. Section 12B: prior approval of the Reserve Bank is mandatory for any person who intends to acquire or agree to acquire, directly or indirectly, shares or voting rights of a banking company which, together with those already held, would entitle the person to five per cent or more of the paid-up share capital or voting rights; transfers of shares are also governed by the Companies Act, 2013; where a bank receives a transfer request taking a party above five per cent it must refer it to the Reserve Bank, which may order the transferee not to exercise voting rights. The aim is that control of banks rests with fit and proper persons. Reports: particulars of shareholding of the Chairman, Managing Director or Chief Executive Officer must be submitted to the Reserve Bank; the Reserve Bank may also order any other information. Section 13 (as amended in 2013): commission, brokerage, discount or remuneration on the sale of shares of a banking company shall not exceed two and a half per cent of the price at which the shares are issued (earlier linked to the paid-up value). Dividend: the courseware states earlier Reserve Bank conditions for declaring a dividend (profit of the current year, minimum capital adequacy and net NPA tests, the bank must comply with Sections 15 and 17, and a payout ratio normally not above 40 per cent). Section 15 prohibits payment of dividend until all capitalised expenses are written off and Section 17 requires transfer of a specified portion of profit to the statutory reserve fund.

Subsidiaries and other companies (courseware): Section 19 restricts the formation of subsidiaries to prevent banks from carrying on trading activities by acquiring a controlling interest in non-banking companies. A bank may form a subsidiary only for: any business permissible to banking companies under Section 6(1) clauses (a) to (o); carrying on the business of banking exclusively outside India (with the Reserve Bank prior permission); and any other business which the Reserve Bank, with the prior approval of the Central Government, considers conducive to the spread of banking in India or otherwise useful or necessary in the public interest. Business undertaken by a subsidiary is not treated as the bank itself taking up that business for Section 8. Under Section 19(2) a bank cannot hold shares in any company as pledgee, mortgagee or absolute owner of an amount exceeding thirty per cent of the paid-up share capital of that company or thirty per cent of its own paid-up share capital and reserves, whichever is less; shares in any company in which its managing director or manager is interested are prohibited except for a subsidiary; a bank may form a subsidiary for credit information business. Section 29A allows the Reserve Bank to order inspection of associate enterprises (holding company, subsidiary, joint venture, or companies exercising control over board composition or significant influence over financial or policy decisions) with Section 35 inspection provisions applying.

Board of directors (courseware): Section 10A requires that at least fifty-one per cent of the total number of directors be persons with special knowledge or practical experience in accountancy, agriculture and rural economy, banking, co-operation, economics, finance, law, small scale industry or any other matter the Reserve Bank considers useful; at least two of the directors must have special knowledge in agriculture and rural economy or co-operation or small scale industry. Substantial interest: a director shall not have substantial interest in a company or firm carrying on trade, commerce or industry as an employee, manager or managing agent (Section 10A(2)(b)); companies under Section 25 of the Companies Act, 1956 (Section 8 of the 2013 Act) and small scale industrial concerns are excluded and proprietors of trading, commercial or industrial concerns other than small scale industrial concerns are also disqualified. Substantial interest is defined in Section 5(ne) by beneficial holding by an individual or spouse or minor child exceeding a fixed sum or ten per cent of the paid-up capital, and in firms by a share exceeding ten per cent of total capital. Period of office: directors other than the chairman or a whole-time director shall not hold office for more than eight years continuously (a removed chairman or whole-time director ceases to be director and is not eligible for further appointment as director for four years). Reconstitution: where a board is not constituted per Section 10A, the Reserve Bank can order reconstitution, if necessary by retirement of directors by lots, and if the bank does not comply within two months the Reserve Bank may remove any director and appoint a new one, whose term would be what the predecessor would have held; no proceedings of a banking company are invalid only because of a defect in the composition of the board.

Chairman and managing director (courseware): Section 10B requires every banking company to have a whole-time or part-time chairman appointed from among its directors; a whole-time chairman manages the entire affairs; a part-time chairman requires prior Reserve Bank approval, and in the absence of a chairman the whole affairs are entrusted to a managing director, subject to superintendence, control and directions of the board. A whole-time chairman and a managing director hold office for not more than five years as the board fixes and are eligible for re-election or reappointment; the whole-time chairman or managing director may continue after the term until the successor assumes office, with Reserve Bank approval. Qualifications (Section 10B(4)): special knowledge and practical experience of the working of a banking company, the State Bank of India or a subsidiary bank or a financial institution, or of financial, economic or business administration; a person is disqualified from a whole-time chairman or managing director post if he or she is a director of any company other than a subsidiary of the bank or a Section 25 company, a partner of a firm carrying on trade, business or industry, has substantial interest in any other company or firm, is a director, manager, managing agent, partner or proprietor of any trading, commercial or industrial concern, or is engaged in any other business or vocation. Removal: if the Reserve Bank thinks the person is not fit and proper it may require the banking company to remove the person and appoint a suitable person, after giving a reasonable opportunity of being heard; failing compliance within two months the Reserve Bank may remove and appoint; appeal lies to the Central Government within thirty days and the Government order, or the Reserve Bank order if no appeal is filed, is final and not challengeable in any civil court. Temporary arrangements for a vacancy caused by death, resignation or incapacity may be made for a period not exceeding four months with Reserve Bank approval. Section 10BB: where the office of chairman or managing director falls vacant and is not filled, the Reserve Bank may appoint a person for a period not exceeding three years, who may be reappointed once and removed by the Reserve Bank, with allowances determined by it. Section 10C exempts the whole-time chairman or managing director from holding qualification shares, and Section 10A directors have a similar exemption. Sections 10A, 10B and 10BB override other laws and contracts and no one affected by action under them has a claim to compensation for loss of office. The Financial Services Institutions Bureau, constituted from 1 July 2022, recommends persons for appointment as whole-time directors and non-executive chairpersons on the boards of financial services institutions and replaces the earlier Banks Board Bureau.

Additional directors, restrictions and Reserve Bank control (courseware): Section 36AB lets the Reserve Bank appoint additional directors to a bank board if in the interest of banking policy, the public or the bank and its depositors it is necessary; such directors hold office at the pleasure of the Reserve Bank for a period not exceeding three years, and further periods not exceeding three years at a time; they incur no liability for acts in good faith, need not hold qualification shares, and are not counted for working out proportions of directors required by the Act. Section 10 restricts employment: a bank shall not employ or continue a managing agent or an employee who is or has been adjudicated insolvent, or suspended payment or compounded with creditors; who has been convicted of an offence involving moral turpitude; whose remuneration is by way of commission or share in profits; or whose remuneration the Reserve Bank considers excessive (the restriction applies to workmen as management personnel per Central Bank of India v Their Workmen, but does not affect bonus under a settlement, or commission paid to brokers or agents who are not regular staff). Persons who are directors of companies other than a subsidiary or a Section 25 / Section 8 company are prohibited from managing a banking company, subject to temporary relaxation allowed by the Reserve Bank. Section 36AA empowers the Reserve Bank to remove any chairman, director, chief executive officer or other officer or employee of a banking company in the public interest, to prevent affairs being conducted detrimentally to depositors, or to secure proper management; before the order the person must have a reasonable opportunity of making a representation, but where urgency demands, the Reserve Bank may bar the person from acting pending consideration. Appeal lies to the Central Government within thirty days of communication, and its decision is final. The removed person ceases to hold office, is prohibited from taking part directly or indirectly in the management of the bank for a period of up to five years as specified, and is punishable for contravention with a fine of Rs 250 for each day of contravention. The Reserve Bank may appoint a suitable person in place for a period not exceeding three years, extendable by further periods of up to three years, who incurs no liability for good faith actions. Section 36ACA allows the Reserve Bank to supersede the board of a banking company for six months, extendable up to twelve months; an Administrator is appointed assisted by a committee of three or more persons and vacates office when the board is reconstituted.

Corporate governance (courseware): the OECD describes the purpose of corporate governance as helping to build an environment of trust, transparency and accountability for long-term investment, financial stability and business integrity. The first major study in India: the Cadbury Committee (UK, 1992); the OECD principles were first published in 1999 and revised in 2004. The six OECD principles (2004): ensuring the basis for an effective corporate governance framework; the rights of shareholders and key ownership functions; the equitable treatment of shareholders (including minority and foreign shareholders); the role of stakeholders; disclosure and transparency; and the responsibilities of the board. Banks hold a special position because they accept and deploy large amounts of public funds in fiduciary capacity and are key to the payment system. The Basel Committee guidance on enhancing corporate governance for banking organisations (February 2006) highlights the roles of boards and senior management (with independent directors), management of conflicts of interest, internal and external auditors and internal control, transparency, and the role of supervisors. In India the Reserve Bank, SEBI and the Department of Company Affairs are concerned. Committees: Dr A.S. Ganguly (Consultative Group, set up in November 2001, report in 2002), Dr R.H. Patil (advisory group on corporate governance, March 2001) and Shri M.S. Verma (advisory group on banking supervision, January 2003). The Reserve Bank introduced the concept of fit and proper criteria for directors (collecting information, due diligence, a nomination committee of the board to scrutinise the declarations). Directors: the board should ensure the responsibilities of directors are well defined and private sector banks should have directors representing specific sectors as provided under the Act; as a matter of desirable practice not more than one member of a family or close relative should be on the board of a bank; the chief executive officer must satisfy the fit and proper criteria; the Reserve Bank may apply additional criteria for the chairman and chief executive. For public sector banks corporate governance principles were statutorily recognised through the Banking Companies (Acquisition and Transfer of Undertakings) and Financial Institutions Laws (Amendment) Act, 2006, which require shareholder directors to be fit and proper persons (Section 9(2)), the Reserve Bank notifying the criteria.

payload.title: Licensing of banking companies (Section 22)
payload.expanded_explanation_md: The seven tests turn the licence into a judgment about depositor safety and system stability, not just a registration.

self_check.prompt_text: Who grants a banking licence and under which section?
self_check.expected_takeaway: The Reserve Bank, under Section 22 of the Banking Regulation Act.

payload.title: Foreign banks, on-tap licensing and cancellation of a licence
payload.core_explanation_md:
**Foreign banks** must show the Reserve Bank that they face **adequate prudential supervision at home** (with regard to **Basel standards**), that the **home regulator approves** the branch or wholly owned subsidiary, and that the home country **does not discriminate** against Indian banks. Other factors: **political and economic relations**, **financial soundness**, **ownership**, **ranking and ratings** and **international presence**.

**Licensing policy (as the courseware tells it):** new bank guidelines in **February 2013**; discussion paper on **continuous authorisation** (**August 2013**); **on tap** licensing guidelines for private sector **universal banks** on **1 August 2016**. Small finance banks: first guidelines in **2014**; on tap guidelines on **5 December 2019**. A **small finance bank** is a **public limited company** under the **Companies Act, 2013**, licensed under **Section 22** and given **scheduled bank** status once it starts operations.

**Cancellation (Section 22(4)):** the Reserve Bank may cancel if the company **stops banking in India** or **fails to meet a licence condition** (normally after giving a chance to comply). **Appeal** to the **Central Government within thirty days**; that decision is **final**.
payload.expanded_explanation_md: On-tap licensing replaced the stop-and-go approach that opened applications only at intervals.

self_check.prompt_text: Within how many days of the decision may a bank appeal against cancellation of its licence?
self_check.expected_takeaway: Thirty days, to the Central Government.

payload.title: Opening and shifting of branches (Section 23)
payload.core_explanation_md:
**Prior Reserve Bank permission** is needed to **open a new place of business** in India or abroad, or to **change the location** of an existing one, **except within the same city, town or village**.

**No permission** is needed for a **temporary place of business** for **up to one month** in a city, town or village (or environs) where the bank already has a place, to give banking facilities at an **exhibition, conference or mela**.

Before granting permission the Reserve Bank may examine **financial condition and history**, **management**, **capital structure and earning prospects**, and whether **public interest** is served; it may attach **conditions** and **revoke** the permission after a hearing if they are broken.

**Place of business** (Section 23(5)) includes a **sub-office, pay office, sub-pay office** or any place where **deposits are received, cheques cashed or money lent**.

**Regional Rural Banks** also get their permission from the Reserve Bank, but applications are **routed through NABARD**.
payload.expanded_explanation_md: The same-city exemption lets a bank move a branch locally without permission, but a move to another town needs approval.

self_check.prompt_text: For how long may a bank run a temporary place of business without permission at an exhibition?

payload.title: Paid-up capital, reserves and capital structure (Sections 11 and 12)
payload.core_explanation_md:
**Section 11** sets **minimum paid-up capital and reserves** for a company wishing to begin banking. The amount depends on the **number of States** and **places of business** and whether **Mumbai or Kolkata** is included. The figures in the courseware are the old statutory scale; this unit teaches the **structure**, not the rupee amounts. A dispute about computing a 'place of business' is settled by the **Reserve Bank**.

**Foreign banks** must **deposit and keep with the Reserve Bank** a prescribed amount in **cash or approved securities**, and also **twenty per cent of each year's profit** from Indian branches; on cessation the deposits become **assets with a first charge for Indian creditors**.

**Section 12(1) capital structure:**

- **Subscribed capital** is **not less than half of authorised capital**.
- **Paid-up capital** is **not less than half of subscribed capital**.
- When capital is raised the test must be met **within two years** (as the Reserve Bank allows).

Banks may issue **equity shares** and **preference shares** (perpetual, irredeemable or redeemable) under **Reserve Bank guidelines**. The **Reserve Bank** has set **separate capital norms** for **small finance** and **universal banks** in its licensing policy.
payload.expanded_explanation_md: The half-and-half tests stop a bank advertising a large authorised capital while collecting little from shareholders.

self_check.prompt_text: What fraction of subscribed capital must be paid up under Section 12(1)?

payload.title: Shareholding, voting rights, commission and dividend
payload.core_explanation_md:
- **Voting cap (Section 12(2)):** no shareholder may vote more than **10 per cent** of total voting rights; the Reserve Bank may **raise the cap in phases to 26 per cent**.
- **Prior approval (Section 12B):** anyone who would hold **5 per cent or more** of **paid-up capital or voting rights** needs **Reserve Bank approval**; a bank that gets a transfer request taking a party over **5 per cent** must refer it. The goal: control stays with **fit and proper** persons.
- **Section 12(3):** a registered shareholder cannot be sued on the ground that title to the shares is with another, except by a **transferee** or on behalf of a **minor or lunatic**.
- **Reports:** shareholding of the **Chairman, MD or CEO** is reported to the Reserve Bank.
- **Section 13:** commission, brokerage or discount on the sale of bank shares is capped at **2.5 per cent of the issue price**.
- **Section 15:** **no dividend** until all **capitalised expenses** are written off; **Section 17:** a specified part of profit goes to the **statutory reserve fund**.

The courseware also states Reserve Bank **conditions on dividends** (current-year profit, capital adequacy and net NPA tests); these are **not taught here** because later directions replaced them.
payload.expanded_explanation_md: The 5 per cent approval limit and the 10 per cent voting cap work together: the first screens who enters, the second limits their say.

self_check.prompt_text: What share of paid-up capital or voting rights needs prior Reserve Bank approval to acquire?

payload.title: Subsidiaries and shareholding in other companies (Sections 19 and 29A)
payload.core_explanation_md:
**Section 19** stops banks from running **trading activities** through **controlling interests in non-banking companies**.

**A bank may form a subsidiary only to:**

1. do any **Section 6(1) business** (clauses (a) to (o));
2. carry on **banking exclusively outside India** (with the Reserve Bank's **prior permission**);
3. do **any other business** the Reserve Bank, with **prior Central Government approval**, finds **conducive to the spread of banking** or in the **public interest**.

Business done by a subsidiary is **not** the bank doing it for **Section 8** purposes.

**Section 19(2):** a bank may not hold shares (as **pledgee, mortgagee or absolute owner**) above **30 per cent of the company's paid-up capital** or **30 per cent of its own paid-up capital and reserves**, **whichever is less**. It may not hold shares in a company in which its **managing director or manager is interested**, except a **subsidiary**.

**Section 29A:** the Reserve Bank can order **inspection of associate enterprises** (holding or subsidiary companies, joint ventures, companies with control over the board or significant influence).
payload.expanded_explanation_md: The 30 per cent ceiling prevents a bank from using pledged or purchased shares to take control of trading companies.

self_check.prompt_text: Under Section 19(2), the 30 per cent share-holding ceiling applies on whichever of two measures is what?
self_check.expected_takeaway: Whichever is less: 30 per cent of the company paid-up capital or 30 per cent of the bank paid-up capital and reserves.

payload.title: Board of directors (Section 10A)
payload.core_explanation_md:
- **At least 51 per cent** of directors must have **special knowledge or practical experience** in **accountancy, agriculture and rural economy, banking, co-operation, economics, finance, law, small scale industry** or another useful field.
- **At least two directors** must have knowledge of **agriculture and rural economy, co-operation or small scale industry**.
- **Substantial interest:** a director must not have **substantial interest** in a company or firm in **trade, commerce or industry** as an **employee, manager or managing agent**. **Section 25 (now Section 8) companies** and **small scale industrial concerns** are excluded; **proprietors of other trading, commercial or industrial concerns** are disqualified. Substantial interest (Section 5(ne)) is a **beneficial holding above a fixed sum or ten per cent of paid-up capital**, and **above ten per cent of capital in a firm**.
- **Term:** directors other than the chairman and whole-time directors may serve **not more than eight years continuously** (courseware, to be checked after the 2025 amendments).
- **Reconstitution:** the Reserve Bank can order it, with **retirement by lots**; if the bank does not comply in **two months** the Reserve Bank may **remove a director and appoint another**. Proceedings are **not invalid** merely because of a **defect in board composition**.
payload.expanded_explanation_md: The 51 per cent rule makes the board a mix of banking and sector expertise rather than only representatives of owners.

self_check.prompt_text: What minimum share of directors must have special knowledge or practical experience?

payload.title: Chairman and managing director (Sections 10B, 10BB and 10C)
payload.core_explanation_md:
**Appointment:** every banking company has a **whole-time or part-time chairman** chosen from its directors; a **whole-time chairman manages the whole affairs**; a **part-time chairman needs prior Reserve Bank approval**. Without a chairman, a **managing director** runs the bank under the **board's control**. **Term:** not more than **five years**, with **re-election** possible; the holder may stay until a successor takes over, with **Reserve Bank approval**.

**Qualifications (Section 10B(4)):** special knowledge of the **working of a bank, SBI, a subsidiary bank or a financial institution**, or of **financial, economic or business administration**. **Disqualifications:** director of another company (other than a subsidiary or Section 25 company), **partner in a trading firm**, **substantial interest** elsewhere, or **engaged in any other business or vocation**.

**Removal:** if the Reserve Bank thinks the person **not fit and proper** it can require the bank to remove and replace, after a **hearing**; if the bank does not act in **two months** the Reserve Bank may remove and appoint. **Appeal** to the **Central Government within thirty days**; the decision is **final**.

**Vacancy:** temporary arrangement for **up to four months** (with Reserve Bank approval); the Reserve Bank may **appoint a chairman for up to three years** (**Section 10BB**), reappointable once. **Section 10C** exempts the chairman or MD from **qualification shares**.

Sections **10A, 10B and 10BB override other laws and contracts** and give **no right to compensation** for loss of office. The **Financial Services Institutions Bureau** (from **1 July 2022**) recommends whole-time directors and non-executive chairpersons, replacing the **Banks Board Bureau**.
payload.expanded_explanation_md: The Reserve Bank can step in at every stage, from the qualification of the chairman to removal and filling a vacancy.

self_check.prompt_text: What is the maximum term of a whole-time chairman or managing director in one appointment?

payload.title: Additional directors, employment limits and the power to remove management
payload.core_explanation_md:
**Additional directors (Section 36AB):** the Reserve Bank may appoint them **in the interest of banking policy or the public interest or of the bank and its depositors**; they serve **at the Reserve Bank's pleasure** for up to **three years** (and further periods of up to three years), are **not liable for good faith acts**, need **no qualification shares**, and are **not counted** in working out the required proportions of directors.

**Restrictions on employment (Section 10):** a bank must not employ or continue a **managing agent or employee** who is **insolvent** (or suspended payment or compounded with creditors), was **convicted of an offence involving moral turpitude**, is paid by **commission or share of profits**, or is paid **excessive** remuneration in the Reserve Bank's opinion. Commission to **brokers and agents outside the regular staff**, and **bonus under a settlement**, are not affected.

**Removal (Section 36AA):** the Reserve Bank may remove a **chairman, director, chief executive officer or any other officer or employee** in the **public interest**, to stop affairs being run **detrimentally to depositors**, or to secure **proper management**.

- The person gets a **reasonable chance to represent**; in **urgent** cases the Reserve Bank may **bar the person pending** a decision.
- **Appeal** to the **Central Government within thirty days**; its decision is **final**.
- The removed person may **not take part in management for up to five years**; a breach attracts a **fine of Rs 250 a day**.
- A **suitable replacement** may be appointed for up to **three years**, extendable by further periods of **up to three years**.

**Supersession (Section 36ACA):** the Reserve Bank can **supersede the board for six months**, extendable up to **twelve months**, with an **Administrator** assisted by a **committee of three or more persons**.
payload.expanded_explanation_md: Supersession is the last step in the ladder, after director removal and additional directors fail to fix the bank.

self_check.prompt_text: For how long may the Reserve Bank first supersede a bank board under Section 36ACA?
self_check.expected_takeaway: Six months, extendable to a maximum of twelve months.

payload.title: Corporate governance and fit and proper criteria
payload.expanded_explanation_md: Fit and proper screening is how the regulator tests the character and competence of those who run and own the bank.

self_check.prompt_text: How many OECD (2004) principles of corporate governance does the courseware list?

payload.stem_md: A company wishes to commence banking business in India. Which authority grants the licence and under which Act?

options.text_md: The Central Government, under the Companies Act
options.explanation_md: The Central Government hears appeals but does not license banks.

options.text_md: SEBI, under the SEBI Act
options.explanation_md: SEBI regulates securities markets and does not license banks.

options.text_md: The Registrar of Companies, under the Companies Act
options.explanation_md: The Registrar incorporates companies; it has no banking licensing role.

options.text_md: The Reserve Bank, under Section 22 of the Banking Regulation Act, 1949
options.explanation_md: Section 22 gives the Reserve Bank the licensing power.

payload.correct_explanation_md: The licence is a Reserve Bank power under the Banking Regulation Act.

payload.stem_md: When the Reserve Bank refuses a licence, the courts will intervene only where

options.text_md: The decision was made on extraneous or unreasonable grounds
options.explanation_md: The courseware says the Reserve Bank has discretion and courts interfere only for such grounds.

options.text_md: The company disagrees with the decision
options.explanation_md: Disagreement alone is not a ground for a court to set aside the decision.

options.text_md: The company has high capital

options.text_md: A person who passed the CAIIB
options.explanation_md: Qualifications are not a bar.

options.text_md: A person who retired from the State Bank
options.explanation_md: Retirement from another bank is not a bar.

options.text_md: A person who has worked in a co-operative bank
options.explanation_md: Co-operative bank experience is not a bar.

payload.correct_explanation_md: Section 10 bars persons with listed disqualifications.

payload.stem_md: Section 36AA empowers the Reserve Bank to remove a chairman, director or other officer

options.text_md: Only after a court conviction
options.explanation_md: A conviction is not required.

options.text_md: In the public interest, to prevent affairs being conducted to the detriment of depositors, or to secure proper management
options.explanation_md: These are the three grounds in the courseware.

options.text_md: Only on the request of shareholders
options.explanation_md: Shareholder request is not required.

options.text_md: Only when the bank is making a loss
options.explanation_md: Loss is not the stated ground.

payload.correct_explanation_md: Section 36AA has three grounds.

payload.stem_md: A person removed by the Reserve Bank under Section 36AA may be prohibited from taking part in the management of the bank for a period of up to

options.text_md: One year
options.explanation_md: One year is shorter than the maximum.

options.text_md: Ten years
options.explanation_md: Ten years exceeds the maximum.

options.text_md: Five years
options.explanation_md: The courseware gives five years.

options.text_md: Life
options.explanation_md: There is no lifetime ban.

payload.correct_explanation_md: The ban is up to five years.

payload.stem_md: The Reserve Bank may supersede the board of a banking company under Section 36ACA for

options.text_md: One month
options.explanation_md: One month is shorter than stated.

options.text_md: Three years
options.explanation_md: Three years exceeds the stated period.

options.text_md: An unlimited period
options.explanation_md: Section 36ACA sets a six month term with a twelve month ceiling.

options.text_md: Six months, extendable up to twelve months in all
options.explanation_md: The courseware gives six months extendable to twelve.

payload.correct_explanation_md: Supersession is time bound.

payload.stem_md: During supersession of a bank board an Administrator is

options.text_md: Appointed and assisted by a committee of three or more persons constituted by the Reserve Bank
options.explanation_md: The courseware gives this arrangement.

options.text_md: Appointed by the shareholders
options.explanation_md: The Reserve Bank appoints.

options.text_md: Appointed by the court
options.explanation_md: The court is not involved.

options.text_md: Appointed from among the old directors
options.explanation_md: The courseware does not require this.

payload.correct_explanation_md: The Reserve Bank appoints the Administrator and committee.

payload.stem_md: Which is one of the six OECD principles of corporate governance (2004)?

options.text_md: Maximisation of profit
options.explanation_md: Profit maximisation is not an OECD principle.

options.text_md: Equitable treatment of shareholders including minority and foreign shareholders
options.explanation_md: The third OECD principle covers this.

options.text_md: Minimisation of tax
options.explanation_md: Tax minimisation is not a principle.

options.text_md: Reduction of the number of directors
options.explanation_md: Board size is not a principle.

payload.correct_explanation_md: Equitable treatment of shareholders is an OECD principle.

payload.stem_md: Why does corporate governance matter more for banks than for most companies?

options.text_md: Are exempt from company law
options.explanation_md: Banks are not exempt from company law.

options.text_md: Pay no tax
options.explanation_md: Tax treatment is not the reason.

options.text_md: They hold large public funds as trustees and operate the payment system
options.explanation_md: The courseware gives these reasons.

options.text_md: Have no shareholders
options.explanation_md: Banks have shareholders.

payload.correct_explanation_md: Public funds and the payment system make governance vital.

payload.stem_md: The Reserve Bank adopted fit and proper criteria for directors on the recommendations of

options.text_md: The Securities Appellate Tribunal
options.explanation_md: The tribunal made no such recommendation.

options.text_md: The Lok Sabha
options.explanation_md: The legislature did not make this recommendation.

options.text_md: The Finance Minister in a speech
options.explanation_md: A speech is not the stated source.

options.text_md: The Ganguly Committee on corporate governance among others
options.explanation_md: The courseware links the criteria to the Ganguly Committee.

payload.correct_explanation_md: The Ganguly group drove the criteria.

payload.stem_md: As a matter of desirable practice, how many members of one family or close relatives should be on the board of a bank?

options.text_md: Not more than one
options.explanation_md: The courseware says not more than one.

options.text_md: Up to half of the board
options.explanation_md: Half is far above the stated practice.

options.text_md: Any number
options.explanation_md: The desirable practice sets a ceiling of one family member or close relative.

options.text_md: At least two
options.explanation_md: The practice is a ceiling, not a minimum.

payload.correct_explanation_md: The desirable practice is one.

payload.stem_md: For public sector banks, what does the Banking Companies (Acquisition and Transfer of Undertakings) and Financial Institutions Laws (Amendment) Act, 2006 require?

options.text_md: All directors to be government officials
options.explanation_md: The Act does not require all directors to be officials.

options.text_md: Shareholder directors to be persons with fit and proper status, with criteria notified by the Reserve Bank
options.explanation_md: The courseware states this.

options.text_md: Directors to be elected by depositors
options.explanation_md: Depositors do not elect directors under the Act.

options.text_md: No directors to be appointed
options.explanation_md: Boards continue to be constituted; the Act only requires shareholder directors to be fit and proper.

payload.correct_explanation_md: The 2006 Act recognised fit and proper criteria.

payload.stem_md: A bank has a board of 12 directors. Section 10A requires at least 51 per cent to have special knowledge or practical experience of the listed subjects. What is the minimum whole number of such directors?

numeric_rule.rounding_instruction: Give a whole number, rounding up to the next whole director.

payload.correct_explanation_md: 51 per cent of 12 is 6.12, so at least 7 directors are needed.

payload.stem_md: A bank has 400 crore total voting rights. A shareholder holds shares carrying 150 crore votes. Counting the ceiling in Section 12(2) at ten per cent, how many crore votes may that shareholder exercise on a poll?
payload.correct_explanation_md: Ten per cent of 400 crore is 40 crore votes.

payload.stem_md: If the Reserve Bank has raised the voting cap to the maximum 26 per cent, how many crore votes out of 400 crore may a shareholder exercise?
payload.correct_explanation_md: 26 per cent of 400 crore = 104 crore.

payload.stem_md: Shares of a bank are issued at Rs 200 each. What is the maximum commission payable per share on its sale under Section 13 at 2.5 per cent of the issue price, in rupees?
payload.correct_explanation_md: 2.5 per cent of Rs 200 = Rs 5.

payload.stem_md: A company has paid-up share capital of Rs 500 crore. A bank has paid-up capital and reserves of Rs 1,200 crore. Under Section 19(2) the bank may hold shares of the company up to 30 per cent of the lesser of the two measures stated. What is the ceiling in crore rupees?
payload.correct_explanation_md: The lesser measure is Rs 500 crore (company paid-up capital), so 30 per cent is Rs 150 crore.

payload.stem_md: A person removed under Section 36AA breaches the order and continues to take part in the management for 12 days. At Rs 250 for each day of contravention, what is the fine in rupees?
payload.correct_explanation_md: 12 days x Rs 250 = Rs 3,000.

payload.stem_md: The Reserve Bank supersedes a bank board for the first term of six months and later extends it to the maximum of twelve months in all. By how many months is the supersession extended?
payload.correct_explanation_md: 12 - 6 = 6 months of extension.

payload.stem_md: A whole-time chairman is appointed for five years from 2021. In which year does the term end if there is no re-election?

numeric_rule.rounding_instruction: Give the year as a whole number.

payload.stem_md: A director other than the chairman has served continuously since 2018. Counting a limit of eight years, in which year must the director leave office?

numeric_rule.rounding_instruction: Give the year as a whole number.
